 :Judgment:

The Petitioners in M.V.C.No.3188/2021 and Mvc.3189/2021 have filed the Petitions against the
Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.50,00,000/
, and Rs.10,0
0,000/ respectively for the death of Balakrishna @ Balakrishnan and injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident

. 
2. Since These Petitions arises out of the same accident and in view of the Order dated 24.02.2022 in MVC No.3189/2021, these two cases were clubbed together and taken for common disposal.

3. The substance of averments made in both the Petitions are as under:
That on 20032021 at about 7.30 p.m. Balakrishna @ Balakrishnan was proceeding by riding the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.TN70H8830 along with pillion rider Prakash on the extreme left side of the road slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations and when they reached near Sampangere border,
Sampangere village, Lakkur hobli, Malur Taluk, Kolar District, at that time, suddenly the driver of Eicher container lorry bearing Reg.No.NL01AD5647 came from Hosur side in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing MVC NO.3189/2021 any of the traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the Two wheeler and caused accident, due to which both rider and pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

3

, even after better and expert treatment to save the life, Balakrishna @
Balakrishnan was succumbed to fatal injuries on the same day at about 9.15 p.m. and the Petitioner in MVC No.3189/2021 took treatment as an inpatient.
4. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner in MVC.3189/2021 was hale and healthy and he was doing Agriculture and business and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/per month.
5. Prior to the date of accident, Balakrishna @ Balakrishnan in MVC.No.3188/2021 was hale and healthy and working as a driver and doing business and was earning Rs.30,000/ per month.

6. The Petitioners in both Petitions have contended that the accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the lorry bearing Reg.No.NL01AD5647 which is owned by the Respondent No.1 and insured with Respondent No.2.
As such both the Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation MVC NO.3189/2021 to the Petitioners.
7. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents in both petitions, the Respondent No.1 did not appear before the court and hence he was placed Exparte.
Respondent No.2 appeared before the Tribunal through its counsel and filed its detailed Objection Statement.
8. In both petitions, Respondent No.2 has denied the age, avocation and the income of the Petitioners and deceased Balakrishna @ Balakrishnan.
Further it denied that the accident has caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Lorry.

Further it has denied the death of Balakrishnan @ Balakrishnan in MVC No.3188/2021 and injuries sustained by the Petitioner in MVC No.3189/2021 in the said accident and the expenses incurred for the treatment of the Petitioner Prakash.
Further it contended that the driver of the offending lorry and rider of motor cycle did not possess valid driving license.
On these grounds, it has prayed to dismiss both the petitions.
9. On the rival pleadings, my Learned Predecessor in office has framed following Issues.
MVC NO.3189/2021 ISSUES IN MVC No.3188/2021 1.
Whether the Petitioner proves that they are the legal representative of the deceased ?

2. Whether the Petitioners prove that Balakrishna @ Balakrishnan S/o Pillappa died due to injuries sustained by him in an accident occurred on 20032021 at about 7.30 p.m. near Sampangere Border, Sampangere village, Lakkur hobli, Malur Taluk, Kolar District, arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Eicher Container Lorry bearing No.NL01AD5647?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
4. What Order or Award ?

On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 did not choose to adduce any evidence.
11. I have heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioners and the learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2.
I have perused the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record.

20. Further, Petitioner in MVC No.3189/2021 has examined Dr.S.A.Somashekara as PW.3 and got marked 2 documents as per Ex.P.22 and 23 i.e., OPD records and Xray of Petitioner and he has reiterated the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.
21. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1 to P.W.3, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 has cross examined the P.W.1 to PW.3 in lengthy.
In the crossexamination PW.1 to PW.3 have denied the suggestions and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the Petitioners.

Though the Respondent No.2 had taken contention that the accident does not caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, it did not lead any evidence to substantiate its contentions.
Moreover, after thorough investigation, the I.O. has filed Chargesheet against driver of the offending lorry.

23. The oral and documentary evidence of P.W.1 to PW.3 and the materials available on record,
clearly shows that the said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the said accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and Balakrishnan in MVC No.3188/2021 was died due to injuries sustained in the accident and Petitioner in MVC No.3189/2021 had sustained injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in MVC No.3188/2021 and Issue No.1 in MVC No.3189/2021 in the "Affirmative".
24. Issue No.1 and 3 in MVC No.3188/2021: Both these issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid the repetition of the facts.

It is stated in the Petition that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased, Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children and Petitioner No.4 and 5 are the parents of the deceased Balakrishna @
Balakrishnan.

In order to prove this fact, PW.1 has produced Aadhaar Cards of the deceased and Sowmiya vs Plot No.175 on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192458726/
7 petitioner No.1 to 5 and Driving Licence of the deceased and got marked Ex.P7 to 13.
Upon going through the same, it clearly shows the relationship of the deceased with the Petitioners.

Hence, the Petitioners have proved that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Balakrishna @ Balakrishnan.
26.
In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 31 years and his avocation is shown as driver and doing business and was earning Rs.30,000/ per month.
In this regard, PW.1 has not produced any documents to prove his income.

Therefore, in the absence of actual income proof, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2021, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e.
15,000/ p.m. is to be taken into consideration MVC NO.3189/2021 for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
27. Further, the PW.1 stated the age of the deceased Balakrishna @ Balakrishnan as 31 years at the time of the accident.

PW.1 has produced Ex.P.7 i.e., the Aadhaar card of the deceased Balakrishna @
Balakrishnan, which shows the date of birth of Balakrishna @ Balakrishnan was 01121990.
The alleged accident was occurred on 20.03.2021.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased Balakrishna @ Balakrishnan was 31 years.

Hence, the age of the deceased Balakrishna @
Balakrishnan to be taken at 31 years for the purpose of calculation.
28. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
MVC NO.3189/2021 29.
The deceased has left behind him, his wife, children and parents.
Hence, the Petitioner No.1 to 5 are considered as dependents.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/ and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/".

As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 is wife, Petitioner No.2 and 3 are children and Petitioner No.4 and 5 are parents of the deceased Balakrishna @ Balakrishnan, the Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rupees 40,000/ towards loss of consortium and Rupees 15,000/ towards loss of estate and Rupees 15,000/ towards funeral expenses.
IV.
COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION, MVC NO.3189/2021 30.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife and she lost her husband's love and care and Petitioner No.2 and 3 are daughter and son of deceased Balakrishna @ Balakrishnan and they lost father's love and care,

Petitioner No.4 and 5 are parents of the deceased Balakrishna @ Balakrishnan and they have lost Sowmiya vs Plot No.175 on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192458726/
8 the love and care of their son in their old age.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
31. The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:
32.
It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was MVC NO.3189/2021 notionally fixed at Rs.15,000/ p.m.

At this juncture, I would like to go through the decision reported in :
1) 2018 ACJ 740, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India At New Delhi in between Manuswamy and others V/s.
Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Trans. Corpn. Ltd, wherein it is held as under:
"Quantum fatal accident Principle of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged :
21, contract worker in a company - High Court did not consider future prospects while computing compensation - Whether claimants are entitled to compensation after addition of 40 per cent of income of the deceased towards future prospects "
 Held :  yes.
2) 2018 ACJ 5, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, at New Delhi in between Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others wherein it is held as under :
"Quantum Fatal accident - Principles of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged 40

9  prospect and make corresponding deduction  towards personal expenses".

The decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that: "In case self employed or person on fixed MVC NO.3189/2021 salary the addition should be 40% below the age of 40 years".

sentences.text: In this Petition, the deceased was aged 31 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 40% of the income has to be added.
So, 40% of Rs.15,000/ comes to Rs.6,000/.

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.21,000/ p.m.
(Rs.15,000/ + Rs.6,000/).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 16.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that where the number of dependent of family members is 4 to 6, 1/4th of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

After deducting 1/4th towards his personal expenses in Rs.21,000/ it comes to Rs.15,750/ (
21,000/  5,250/) and multiplier applied is 16 which comes to Rs.30,24,000/ (15,750/ x 12 =
1,89,000/, Rs.1,89,000/ x 16 = Rs.30,24,000/).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for MVC NO.3189/2021 compensation of Rs.30,24,000/ towards loss of dependency.

33. TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:
1. Loss of consortium Rs. 40,000/
2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 15,000/
5. Expenses of transportation Rs. 5,000/ of dead body 6.

Loss of Dependency Rs.30,24,000/ Total Rs.31,49,000/ Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.31,49,000/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

: As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending lorry by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.

sentences.text: In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 23 years.
The Petitioner has produced Aadhaar Card i.e., Ex.P.16 shows the date of birth of the Petitioner as 08.08.1998.
The accident took place on 20.03.2021.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner is 23 years at the time of accident.

Hence, the same is to be taken for the purpose of assessment.
36.
Further, the Petitioner has averred that he was doing agricultural and business and was earning Rs.25,000/ per month.
In this regard, he has not produced any documents to prove the income.

Therefore, in the absence of any documentary evidence, this Court is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2021, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e. 15,000/ p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
37.
With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:

38 . The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P14 and other medical MVC NO.3189/2021 records reveals that in the accident the petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1. Swelling and tenderness present in the right wrist and forearm 2. Multiple abrasions over the face 3. Tenderness and abrasions over both leg 4. Tenderness and swelling on the left shoulder
Further, the Doctor has opined that said injury No.1 and 4 are grievous and injury No.2 and 3 are simple in nature.
Further, P.W.3 has also reiterated about the grievous injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident.
39. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
40.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.25,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
MVC NO.3189/2021 III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
41. The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient for 8 days at M.V.J. Medical College and Research Hospital, Bengaluru.

42.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/ under this head (@ Rs.15,000/ per month ).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
43.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and MVC NO.3189/2021 circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/ (@ Rs.100/ per day) towards attendants charges,
Rs.6,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/ under this head.

V.
COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
44. The Petitioner has produced 33 medical bills at Ex.P.17 amounting to Rs.36,112/.
I have gone through the medical bills.
The bill at Sl.No.30 is duplicate bill.
The acceptable medical bills totally comes to Rs.34,412/.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.34,450/ as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
45. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he cannot work.

46. Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr. MVC NO.3189/2021 Somashekara as P.W.3 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident he made.
Further, he got marked OPD card and Xray at Ex.P.22 and Ex.P.23.
He assessed the disability of right upper limb at 39% and whole body disability of the Petitioner at 19%.
47. Even in his evidence, he has reiterated the same.
He has denied the suggestions putforth to him by the Learned Counsel for Petitioner.
In the crossexamination he admitted that he has not personally treated the Petitioner and he has examined the Petitioner for the purpose of assessing the disability.
Further he admitted that fractures are united.

48. Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on record and evidence of P.W.3 and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 10% would be just and proper.

Sowmiya vs Plot No.175 on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192458726/
12 49.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 18.

With multiplier of 18, income of Rs.15,000/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with MVC NO.3189/2021 respect to his whole body at 10%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.3,24,000/
(Rs.15,000/ x 12 = 1,80,000/, Rs.1,80,000/x 18 x 10/100=3,24,000/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,24,000/ under this head.

COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
50.
The doctor i.e., PW.3 has deposed that the Petitioner needs removal of implants which approximately cost about 30,000/.
